answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and isolated to the primary region; rollback is forbidden by the security-patch constraint, so memory_b1 is relevant only as a ruled-out path. Circuit breaking (memory_b4) fails requests and would drop customer writes. Read-replica routing (memory_b5) offloaded report/read traffic, not the write path under settlement load. That leaves region-scoped mitigation: memory_b2 is the closest prior (failover restored latency with a clean shift). memory_b3 (pre-peak headroom) is the main alternative but the surge is already underway, so it is the second archive check rather than the current intent. Settlement is at daily peak, so shifting writes can put downstream money-movement at risk and is flagged. Secondary-region code level vs the unrevertable patch is unknown; treat failover efficacy and patch-exposure as unverified until b2/b3 archives return.
